finding: The round-2 revision replaced the non-`spec-coverage` streak justification with a new one that reverts the finding it was meant to fix, and contradicts its own closing sentence. New text: "A lens that has been quiet for five rounds and one that broke a five-round streak this round are the same in `open` and different in `consecutive_clean`, and that difference is what tells a driver whether a repair has just regressed something or a known backlog is simply still there." Both halves are false under §2.2's own definitions. (a) `role_streaks` entries are only the roles with rows in the latest round, and a role is clean in a round iff every one of its rows is PASS, so `open == 0` iff `consecutive_clean >= 1`: a lens quiet for five rounds has open 0 / cc 5, one that broke its streak this round has open > 0 / cc 0 — they are NOT "the same in `open`". (b) "a repair has just regressed something" and "a known backlog is simply still there" both mean open > 0, hence cc = 0 for both — the exact conflation the accepted round-2 finding proved `consecutive_clean` cannot resolve, restated in new words. The paragraph's own last sentence concedes it: "For a role that holds open rows in the latest round the streak is necessarily 0, and carries no information beyond `open > 0`."

finding: §1 item 1 promises the signal fires when spec-coverage has been clean for the required number of rounds "against an unchanged spec", but §2.4 condition 3 pins staleness to engine.StateStale, which compares only the LATEST recorded round's spec_hash against the current hash. Nothing in §2.2 or §2.4 says whether the rounds inside the walked segment must share a spec hash, and §6 test 14 covers only an edit made after the last recorded round. Two engineers write opposite tests for a mid-streak edit: one asserts divergence is suppressed, the other asserts it fires.

finding: §3.1 makes entry validity behaviorally significant — an entry the validator rejects does not retire the suggestion — and §3.3 adds `mechanized_classes` so that a class which VANISHES from the candidate list is explained. Nothing covers the opposite surprise, which is the more likely one: a driver who registered a check and still sees its class in `mechanize_candidates` under the register-a-check hint. §3.1's reassurance ("A failing check is already reported in `mechanical_checks` and already gates the exit code of `tp review --status --check`") covers failing checks, not invalid ones. In code an invalid entry is skipped inside `runMechanicalChecks` with an `output.Notice` (internal/cli/review_status.go:182-184), which runs ONLY under `--check`; the plain `tp review <spec> --status` path builds `mechanical_checks` from `registeredChecksList` (review_status.go:158-164), which lists every entry with no validity marker and emits no advisory. So on §3.2 mode 2 without `--check` the same payload shows the class as registered AND as an unsuppressed candidate, with nothing naming the reason — the guess-the-cause state §1 says this release exists to remove.

"Above" is directionally ambiguous over a round sequence: in the oldest-first ordering used everywhere else in the spec and in state.json it reads as "older", which is the opposite of what the test needs — the streak-closing round must lie BETWEEN the deleted round and the latest round for the walk to stop before reaching the deleted one. Built the other way the walk legitimately reaches round 2, the advisory fires, and this discriminating boundedness test fails against a correct implementation.
